FROM A REAL SOURCE TO A CLEAR PICTURE

Bring your own evidence.

Import historical telemetry, collect actual disk readings, or inspect a local folder.

Historical telemetry

CSV columns: server, day, used_gb, capacity_gb. At least 3 timestamps per server; 10 for validation metrics.

Real disk collector

Run python3 collector.py locally. It stores actual volume readings in SQLite and exports compatible CSV.

Inspect a folder

Choose a folder to measure actual file sizes in this browser. Files stay on your device. No disk-total claim.

Collect, then import

python3 collector.py --path . --once
python3 collector.py --path . --interval 60
python3 collector.py --export telemetry.csv

Press Ctrl+C to stop collection. Each point is a measured sample with elapsed days, not a fabricated day of history. Short sessions cannot establish a reliable daily trend. The default database is local storage-history.sqlite3.

OPEN THE BLACK BOX

A forecast you can explain.

Ordinary least squares, evaluated against unseen later observations.

Train on the past. Test on the future.

How the forecast is produced

  1. Split chronologically: first 78% for training, remaining 22% for testing.
  2. Compare held-out predictions with actual observations; compute MAE and RMSE.
  3. Refit on all observations for the deployed slope; anchor the forecast to the latest measurement.
  4. Estimate threshold crossings and a normal-approximation 95% prediction interval.

Honest about uncertainty.

The initial dataset is synthetic. High scores on this dataset do not establish real-world accuracy.

The interval assumes independent residuals with constant variance and a continuing linear trend. Workload changes, retention jobs and sudden imports can break those assumptions.

Only 3 samples are needed to fit a line, but that does not make a short collection session a dependable daily forecast.

No paid AI API · no hidden model calls
